page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 6455B cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a high base clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes a 60 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scores reaching 2226.0 and single-threaded gzip compression processing at 34.55 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Text processing performance is particularly notable, scoring 2903.0 in Geekbench, which ranks in the top 10%. Multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally align with average performance tiers, showing a multi-core Geekbench score of 8490.0 and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 70.75 GB/sec. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7iz.2xlarge delivers a high-frequency compute profile paired with a dense DDR5 memory configuration, making it a viable option for workloads requiring high per-core performance without the overhead of scaling to larger instance sizes. However, the lack of bundled local storage means users must rely on external network-attached storage, which may impact overall I/O-heavy workloads. This instance is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, text processing, and workloads utilizing specialized vector or matrix instructions.
